data.one_liner: Pure‑dart PDF parser that reads PDF structures from a byte stream.
data.what_it_does: It parses PDF files into a document object model, exposing catalogs, pages, outlines and other PDF objects. It works on all supported platforms, including web, by using a byte stream abstraction.
use_when: You need to read PDF metadata or extract pages without rendering the PDF.
You want a lightweight, pure‑dart solution that works on web and mobile.
You need to process PDFs in a serverless or CLI environment without native dependencies.
avoid_when: You need to render PDFs to the screen or display them in a widget.
You require advanced PDF manipulation like editing or signing.
You need a full PDF viewer with UI components.
strengths: Pure Dart, no native dependencies; works on web, mobile, desktop.
Supports badly formatted PDFs and compressed cross‑reference tables.
Provides a clear API for accessing catalog, pages, outlines, and page objects.
Good test coverage and CI integration.
weaknesses: No rendering or UI support; only parsing.
Limited to reading; no editing or annotation features.
Performance may be slower for very large PDFs compared to native libraries.
Requires manual handling of file streams on each platform.
data.setup_notes: Add dependency in pubspec and import 'dart_pdf_reader.dart'. No special permissions needed.
